content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to decrease the data being sent between the web browser and [product_name] [version_no]? My wireless connection struggles with the current amount of transmitted information, causing timeouts for both [product_name] [version_no] and the browser. For example, when I open Edge, no data is sent at first, but after logging in, a huge data exchange occurs—transferring graphics, characters, etc. Even once everything appears loaded for [product_name] [product_name_operator_device], data continues to flow and the system remains idle for me, with long waits and ongoing communication. Why is this happening? Ideally, pressing F2 on the [product_name_operator_device] in Edge should only send the related data to [product_name] [version_no] with a return message to my PC and the device. Basic tests like pinging between browser and [product_name] [version_no] result in very slow response times—pinging with 64 bytes at 1,200 ms (1.2 sec) for 60 kbit/s wireless, and 800 ms for 120 kbit/s. It's not feasible to keep transmitting constantly. The 868 MHz ISM band allows up to 10% transmission time (0.1 sec every second). My setup includes two interface converters ([product_name] [article_no]) and two wireless modules ([product_name] [article_no]). The IT department restricts the use of 2.4 GHz (and 5 GHz?) bands, and blacklisting is not permitted. Best regards from [user_name], Sweden.

This forum is meant for users to share experiences and help each other—it is not formal support from [company_name]. If you need official support, please initiate a request using the "Support Request" button at the top menu and follow the instructions provided.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faces excessive, ongoing data transfer between their web browser and [product_name] [version_no] over a wireless link with strict bandwidth and transmission time limits. This results in long response times and inefficient operation, as large amounts of unnecessary data are exchanged even without active user interaction. The situation is frustrating since only specific actions should trigger communication, not constant streaming.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects communication between the web browser and [product_name] [version_no] to be minimal and only occur when necessary, such as when specific user actions are performed—rather than continuous transmission of superfluous data.
